key_concept: Each turn of the Calvin cycle fixes one $CO_2$, and one glucose ($C_6H_{12}O_6$) needs 6 carbons, so it requires 6 turns.
steps: One turn of the Calvin cycle fixes one molecule of $CO_2$ (one carbon) onto RuBP via RuBisCO.
One glucose molecule, $C_6H_{12}O_6$, contains 6 carbon atoms, so it needs 6 $CO_2$ to be fixed.
Turns per glucose $= 6$. This consumes $18\,ATP$ and $12\,NADPH$.
Equivalently, carbons needed $= 3 \times 6 = 18$ $CO_2$, which means 18 turns.
why_not_others: Option (1), 6, is the number of turns for only one glucose. Option (2), 3, simply repeats the number of glucose molecules. Option (3), 1, wrongly assumes one turn makes a whole glucose.
common_trap: Students often answer 6, recalling '6 turns per glucose' without multiplying by the 3 glucose molecules asked.
time_saving_tip: Count carbons: turns = total C atoms in the product = $3 \times 6 = 18$.
